mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above 4.25% in the month preceding the decision date is associated with a short-term discount rate shock that reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4.25% in the month prior to decision_date
regime_hint: early stage of a tightening cycle
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in similar tightening episodes are not statistically lower than in pre-tightening periods (two-tailed t-test, p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the 12-month change in CPIAUCSL exceeds +2% in a month, it reflects accelerating inflation expectations that compress real equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Over 60-day window following such a month, 20-day forward returns are not statistically worse than in the month before the inflation surprise (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly rise in PAYEMS of at least 2,000 jobs accompanied by a concurrent decline in UNRATE below 5% signals a strengthening labor market that boosts corporate earnings expectations, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by ≥2,000 in a month AND UNRATE falls below 5% in the same month
failure_condition: In analogous labor market strengthening episodes, the 20-day forward return is not statistically higher than during labor market weakness (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive 2-month decline in GDPC1 above 3% of the prior month's value indicates weakening business fixed-investment demand, which reduces growth prospects and is associated with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 falls for two consecutive months by >3% relative to prior month
failure_condition: In comparable demand weakness episodes, the 60-day forward return is not significantly worse than in robust investment periods (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in INDPRO (≥10% month-over-month decline) following a period of expansion signals supply-side headwinds that compress production capacity, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by ≥10% MoM after at least one prior month of expansion
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns during comparable supply shocks are not statistically lower than during normal periods (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS remains above 5% for three consecutive months, it signals persistent policy tightness that raises real risk-free rates and dampens equity risk premia, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: In similar prolonged high-rate regimes, 20-day forward returns are not statistically worse than during normal periods (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden spike in HOUST (≥10% month-over-month increase) accompanied by a decline in UNRATE below 6% indicates a surge in consumer demand that boosts earnings expectations, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by ≥10% MoM AND UNRATE falls below 6% in the same month
failure_condition: In analogous demand spikes, the 20-day forward return is not statistically higher than in neutral periods (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A regime shift to persistent supply-side easing (defined by two consecutive months of RSAFS falling by >5% from prior month) lowers real wage growth expectations and is associated with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS falls by >5% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: During comparable supply easing episodes, the 60-day forward return is not statistically lower than during supply contraction (p > 0.05).
